title: felhív, kikapcsol, bekapcsol: Prefixes on the Phone

sections.title: Direction words on a phone
sections.content: You know the direction prefixes *be-* (in), *ki-* (out), *fel-* (up) and *le-* (down) from A1 (*bemegy*, *kimegy*, *felmegy*). On a phone they become everyday verbs: *felhív* ("to phone someone", literally "call up"), *bekapcsol* ("to switch on") and *kikapcsol* ("to switch off"). Two things you already know still hold. With *-lak/-lek* (Unit 38) the prefix stays in front: *felhívlak* ("I'll phone you"). In a command (Unit 10) the prefix steps behind the verb: *Hívd fel Katát!*, *Kapcsold ki a mobilt!*

items.spanish: A moziban mindig kikapcsolom a mobilomat.
items.english: In the cinema I always switch off my phone.

sections.content: Do not split the prefix in a plain statement: say *Felhívom Katát*, not *Fel hívom Katát*. The prefix only steps behind the verb in a command like *Hívd fel!*
